overview: This database is designed to manage and organize academic research data, including publications, authors, and organizations. It also tracks bibliographic relationships such as citations, authorship, and keyword associations. Furthermore, it categorizes these academic entities into various research domains.
areas: Research categorization: domain, domain_author, domain_conference, domain_journal, domain_keyword, domain_publication
notes: The author table uses aid as the primary identifier and oid potentially for organization linkage.
The publication table links to conferences via cid and journals via jid.
Mapping tables like domain_author, domain_conference, domain_journal, and domain_keyword relate entities to domains using did.
The domain_publication table links domains (did) to publications (pid).
The publication_keyword table links publications (pid) to keywords (kid).
The writes table links authors (aid) to publications (pid).
The cite table links citing publications to cited publications using publication IDs.

tables.author: Stores author details including their identification, name, and homepage.
tables.conference: Stores conference details including identification, name, and homepage.
tables.domain: Stores domain information with an identifier and name.
tables.domain_author: Links authors to their respective domains.
tables.domain_conference: Links conferences to their respective domains.
tables.journal: Stores journal details including identification, name, and homepage.
tables.domain_journal: Links journals to their respective domains.
tables.keyword: Stores keywords with an identifier and text.
tables.domain_keyword: Links keywords to their respective domains.
tables.publication: Stores publication details such as title, abstract, year, and metrics.
tables.domain_publication: Stores the association between domains and publications using their respective IDs.
tables.organization: Stores details about organizations including their name, homepage, continent, and organization ID.
tables.publication_keyword: Stores the relationship between publications and keywords using their IDs.
tables.writes: Stores which authors wrote which publications using author and publication IDs.
tables.cite: Stores citation relationships between cited publications and citing publications using publication IDs.
